discoveries.mechanism: Expiry-day two-patch index path: SEBI documented aggressive constituent buying 09:15-11:46 (index lifted) then aggressive selling 11:49-close into a net-short options book. Tests whether on monthly-opex days the morning index move systematically reverses into the close on Fusion index CFDs (dealer/option-book unwind). The India pattern was manipulation by one dominant player; transfer to US/EU expiry is an untested hypothesis.

discoveries.mechanism: 'Extended marking the close': SEBI found aggressive selling in the final 60 minutes (from 14:30) to depress the closing level that settles options. Retail-usable form: abnormal last-hour displacement into a settlement close tends to be flow, not information, and partially reverses next session. Existing family; add an expiry-day-only variant via the conditioner gap below.

Trade fades of large intraday displacements in S&P/Nasdaq CFDs when liquidity is high.

discoveries.mechanism: Avellaneda-Lee PCA residual stat-arb transplanted to an FX-majors panel: remove top principal components (USD factor, risk factor) over a 60-trading-day window (=1440 H1 bars), model residual as OU, enter at |s|>1.25, exit near 0.5-0.75. The D.E. Shaw/PDT/Citadel stat-arb template (Citadel's HFT 'grew out of' stat-arb).
discoveries.evidence: DOCUMENTED (construction and backtest on US equities); FX transfer SPECULATED
discoveries.source_title: Avellaneda & Lee (2009) Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market
discoveries.quote: We select as entry point for trading any residual that deviates by 1.25 standard deviations from equilibrium

discoveries.mechanism: Same PCA residual construction on precious/base metals (gold, silver, platinum, palladium, copper): first PC = metals/USD factor; trade idiosyncratic residual reversion.
discoveries.source_title: Avellaneda & Lee (2009) Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market

discoveries.mechanism: Avellaneda-Lee 'trading time': divide the daily move by relative volume so contrarian bets favour moves on LOW volume and avoid betting against high-volume prints. 24h z-scored return / (activity / 240h mean activity), negated.

discoveries.quote: It amounts to buying losers and selling winners w.r.t. the market index

discoveries.mechanism: 151 Strategies §10.3.1 contrarian with market-activity filter: fade the weekly move only where weekly volume rose (larger volume changes indicate greater overreaction). Tick-activity proxy for volume; open-interest leg unavailable.
discoveries.source_title: Kakushadze & Serur (2018) 151 Trading Strategies, SSRN 3247865 (Springer book edition later retracted)
discoveries.quote: larger volume changes are likely indicative of greater overreaction

discoveries.mechanism: Kakushadze's intraday mean-reversion alpha is built on the overnight (close-to-next-open) return with a 4-factor model; the overnight return reverts intraday. Index CFDs: fade the cash-session gap.
discoveries.source_title: Kakushadze (2014) Mean-Reversion and Optimization, arXiv:1408.2217

discoveries.mechanism: WQ Alpha#54 ~ -(close-low)/(high-low)*(open/close)^5: fade position within the day's range (the (open/close)^5 factor ~1 on H1/FX). Daily semantics via 24-bar high/low.

discoveries.source_title: Kakushadze (2015) 101 Formulaic Alphas, arXiv:1601.00991
discoveries.quote: Alpha#54: ((-1 * ((low - close) * (open^5))) / ((low - high) * (close^5)))

discoveries.mechanism: WQ Alpha#18: -rank(stddev(|close-open|,5) + (close-open) + corr(close,open,10)); fade bars where body volatility and open/close co-movement are high. Body term dropped to satisfy grammar depth; sign via fade.
discoveries.source_title: Kakushadze (2015) 101 Formulaic Alphas, arXiv:1601.00991
discoveries.quote: Alpha#18: (-1 * rank(((stddev(abs((close - open)), 5) + (close - open)) + correlation(close, open, 10))))

discoveries.quote: Alpha#38: ((-1 * rank(Ts_Rank(close, 10))) * rank((close / open)))

discoveries.quote: Alpha#34: rank(((1 - rank((stddev(returns, 2) / stddev(returns, 5)))) + (1 - rank(delta(close, 1)))))

discoveries.mechanism: WQ Alpha#43: ts_rank(volume/adv20,20) * ts_rank(-delta(close,7),8): buy recent losers when relative volume is high (capitulation reversal). Tick activity as volume proxy.

discoveries.quote: Alpha#43: (ts_rank((volume / adv20), 20) * ts_rank((-1 * delta(close, 7)), 8))

discoveries.mechanism: WQ Alpha#7: only when volume > adv20, fade the 7-bar move scaled by its 60-bar rank of magnitude (large moves on heavy activity fade).

discoveries.mechanism: D.E. Shaw: the negative stock-bond correlation regime rests on anchored inflation; if inflation unanchors the correlation snaps positive. A break of the rolling US500/UST10Y correlation is a regime signal (condition gold/duration sleeves on it).
discoveries.source_title: D. E. Shaw Market Insights: Positively Negative - Stock-Bond Correlation (2019)
discoveries.quote: markets could snap back to a regime of positive correlations, potentially pushing the term premium much higher.

discoveries.mechanism: D.E. Shaw gold note: gold's portfolio utility rises when stocks and bonds are positively correlated. Trade gold's weekly trend only while the risk/rates driver correlation is positive (sign convention of the 'rates' terminal must be checked before judging).
discoveries.source_title: D. E. Shaw: Worth Its Weight? Assessing Gold's Portfolio Utility (2025)
discoveries.quote: in a positive stock-bond correlation environment, the potential portfolio utility of gold increases, even if our forecast for gold remains unchanged.

discoveries.mechanism: Two Sigma GMM regime model (Crisis / Steady State / Inflation / Walking-on-Ice) gives per-period regime probabilities; 'Walking on Ice' tends to precede/follow Crisis. Use the existing HMM/regime family on multi-asset CFDs; leaving-probability as trigger.

discoveries.mechanism: Virtu: volatility widens spreads because takers pay more to transact - the liquidity provider's gain. Retail-side proxy: after a spread spike with a large move, the move was liquidity-driven and mean-reverts as spread normalises (liquidity provision in time).

discoveries.source_title: Virtu Financial, Inc. Form S-1 (2015)
discoveries.quote: Increases in market volatility can cause bid/ask spreads to widen as market participants are willing to incur greater costs to transact, which we benefit from.

discoveries.mechanism: PDT (Muller): short-horizon edge comes from providing temporal liquidity to over-trading institutions. Fade abnormal displacement that fails to continue (the over-trading footprint).

discoveries.quote: shorter horizon strategies get their edge from providing temporal liquidity to a market place or predicting short-term trends that arise from inefficient trading
